plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate limits.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero.
This aligns with capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
Focus on income and broad index for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure, aiming for lower drawdown. Expect reduced volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet mandate limits and reduce concentration.
Reduce all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to smaller positions.
This reduces overall leverage while maintaining some exposure.
Buy DRIP at 4% as a strong scanner long setup to add growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-scoring long setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet mandate limits and reduce concentration.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to 6% each.
This strategy leans into existing tech exposure and uses leverage for growth.
Buy DRIP at 6% as a strong scanner long setup, further concentrating in high-potential areas.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leveraged ETF exposure and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown risk and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize income generation.
This strategy focuses on monthly distributions and low drawdown.
The goal is to park cash for yield with reduced growth focus.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It significantly reduces high-beta and leveraged exposure for lower drawdown. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market downturns.
